summary.headline: School Committee reviews multi-million dollar Neary renovation options, reports $2 million surplus on roof work, and amends teacher contract.
summary.summary: The Southborough School Committee received updates on elementary building projects, including a Neary roof project running under budget with nearly $2 million expected to be returned to the town, while reviewing renovation options for Neary ranging up to $36 million. The committee also evaluated school improvement action plans, previewed upcoming capital requests including plumbing and fencing upgrades, and approved FY28 budget priorities. Following an executive session, the committee voted to amend the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A contract to align its salary schedule with Algonquin starting in July 2027.

topics.title: Food services update and new management
topics.summary: District food service vendor Whitsons introduced its new general manager, Christina Blake, and reported on recent kitchen initiatives across the district. Administrators highlighted the addition of a dedicated chef manager, successful specialty meal promotions including middle school sushi and district-wide halal tacos, and expanding breakfast participation.
key_details: Christina Blake was introduced as the new general manager for Whitsons overseeing all 10 district schools.
Chef manager Mike Holding joined August 17 to support daily kitchen operations and staff training.
Trottier Middle School served roughly 250 sushi rolls during a guest-chef promotion.
Halal-certified beef tacos were served district-wide with strong positive community feedback.
Breakfast participation at Woodward increased from a few students daily to approximately 40 per day.
topics.outcome: Information presented; committee members asked questions regarding meal offerings and kitchen staffing.

topics.title: School principals monthly reports
topics.summary: Principals from Finn, Woodward, Neary, and Trottier shared monthly highlights including school assemblies, community events, and curriculum launches. Activities ranged from cross-grade student groups and walking school buses to a fifth-grade principal-for-a-day fundraiser and new sixth-grade science modules.
key_details: Finn Elementary launched Finn Families cross-grade groups and monthly birthday lunch celebrations.
Woodward School raised $18,970 toward its $20,000 Color Run goal and hosted its first walking school bus with over 20 students.
Neary Elementary held its Great Neary Wizard Challenge with 15 collaborative stations and a student principal-for-a-day event.
Trottier Middle School held its Welcome Back Dance with more than 250 students and implemented the Amplify Science curriculum in sixth grade.

topics.title: Elementary school improvement action plans
topics.summary: Elementary principals presented Year 3 of the 2024-2027 school improvement plans aligned with the district Vision 2032 strategic framework. The plan emphasizes foundational literacy, collaborative data analysis using the Open Architects platform, restorative justice practices, and social-emotional wellness.
key_details: Foundational reading programs include Letterland for Pre-K, UFLI for K-3, and Handwriting Without Tears.
The district replaced AnalyticVue with Open Architects to give teachers faster, more reliable data analysis tools.
Instructional coaching cycles in math and literacy are underway to model lessons directly in classrooms.
Schools are administering a student belonging and connection survey this year to establish baseline culture metrics.
Social-emotional learning continues with the Second Step curriculum and SAEBRS screening.
topics.outcome: Principals presented Year 3 updates; a new three-year plan will be developed next year.

topics.title: Routine business
topics.summary: The committee addressed routine administrative business including acceptance of a gift, committee liaison assignments, revolving fund tracking, warrants, personnel appointments, and meeting minutes.
key_details: Accepted an anonymous donation of $85 to the Southborough Extended Day Program.
Appointed member Kelly Conklin as liaison to the Elementary School Building Committee.
Reviewed monthly revolving funds, payrolls, warrants, and personnel notifications.
Approved open meeting minutes of September 9 and October 2, 2026, and executive session minutes of September 9, 2026.
topics.outcome: Routine motions approved by unanimous votes.

topics.title: Neary and Trottier roof projects and Finn floor assessment
topics.summary: District administration provided progress updates on three major building infrastructure projects across town schools. The Neary roof replacement is nearly 90 percent complete with substantial cost savings, the Trottier MSBA roof project has advanced to 60 percent design, and an engineering evaluation is starting on the Finn School flooring.
key_details: Neary roof replacement is close to 90 percent complete, with final demobilization expected by mid-November.
Of the $4.5 million Town Meeting appropriation for the Neary roof, the district anticipates returning nearly $2 million to the town.
Trottier roof replacement submitted 60 percent design to MSBA; bidding may begin as early as Thanksgiving with construction planned for summer 2027.
RGB Architects was awarded a $95,000 contract using funds from the $810,000 Finn flooring appropriation to conduct moisture testing and conditions assessments.
A formal report on the Finn floor conditions is expected in early 2027, with construction potentially scheduled for summer 2027.
topics.outcome: Updates accepted; Neary project remains on schedule and significantly under budget.
topics.why_it_matters: School roofing and flooring projects involve millions of dollars in taxpayer funds, and returning nearly $2 million from the Neary roof reduces the town's borrowing burden.

topics.title: Elementary school building committee project options for Neary
topics.summary: Superintendent Gregory Martineau reported on options being evaluated by the Elementary School Building Committee for Neary School ahead of an architect presentation. The committee is weighing whether to pursue a phased base upgrade, a comprehensive modernization, or a larger addition/renovation project, as well as whether to reapply to the MSBA.
key_details: Tappe Architects will present detailed plans to the building committee covering three project tiers.
Option 1 involves spending the remaining $12 million of a $15 million baseline target on essential safety, fire suppression, and ADA upgrades.
Option 2 is a full building systems modernization estimated between $28 million and $30 million.
Option 3 is a comprehensive addition and renovation estimated between $35 million and $36 million to fully support modern educational spaces.
The committee will discuss in November whether to submit an MSBA Statement of Interest, which would restart the state funding process and take five to six years.
topics.outcome: Information presented ahead of the building committee's October 15 meeting; the School Committee will discuss MSBA submission options in November.
topics.why_it_matters: The decision on how to upgrade or renovate Neary School carries major long-term tax implications and dictates elementary school facility quality for decades.

topics.title: FY27 first quarter budget and line-item transfers
topics.summary: Director of Finance and Operations Rebecca Pellegrino presented the FY27 general fund expenditure report through September 30, 2026. The budget has an available balance of $349,347, or 1.34 percent of the operating budget, after accounting for two additional elementary teachers hired to address class sizes.
key_details: First quarter available budget balance stood at $349,347 (1.34 percent of operating budget).
The budget absorbed two newly hired elementary teachers added over the summer to maintain target class sizes.
Four budget line items showed deficits: curriculum/department head salaries, generator fuel, water, and special education transportation.
Transfers were identified within existing budget lines to cover the overages without requiring additional funds.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 4-0 to accept the first-quarter general fund expenditure report and approve the FY27 budget line-item transfers.

topics.title: FY28 capital plan preview
topics.summary: Assistant Superintendent Keith Lavoie presented a preview of upcoming capital requests for FY28 and future fiscal years. Priority requests for FY28 include replacing obsolete circular birdbath-style student wash sinks at Trottier and Finn, as well as addressing deteriorating fencing and stormwater retention at Finn School.
key_details: Replacement of antiquated birdbath-style sinks at Finn and Trottier is estimated at $360,000 total due to unavailable replacement parts.
Finn School parking lot fencing and retention area remediation is budgeted at $100,000 in FY28.
Future out-year capital projects will note whether they are candidates for MSBA Accelerated Repair reimbursement.
The committee agreed to wait to vote on the capital plan until Neary building recommendations are finalized.
topics.outcome: Discussion held; capital plan will return for a formal vote after building committee recommendations are clarified.

topics.title: FY28 budget priorities approval
topics.summary: The committee reviewed and voted to approve the FY28 budget priorities developed by the budget subcommittee. These guidelines will direct administration in building the upcoming fiscal year operating budget.
key_details: Priorities were updated from FY27 following review by the budget subcommittee.
The guidelines will govern the administration's preliminary budget build presented in November.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 5-0 to approve the FY28 School Committee budget priorities as presented.

topics.title: Policy J-220: Medication Administration in Schools
topics.summary: The committee conducted a second reading and final review of updated Policy J-220 governing medication administration in schools. The revised policy was previously reviewed by the policy subcommittee and submitted for combined committee review.
key_details: Policy J-220 establishes rules and procedures for school nurses administering medications to students.
The update completes a review process initiated during the prior school year.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 5-0 to approve Policy J-220 as presented.

topics.title: Collective bargaining contract amendment for Unit A
topics.summary: Following an executive session, the committee reconvened in open session and voted to amend the collective bargaining agreement with the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A. The amendment adjusts retirement incentive provisions and aligns Southborough's teacher salary schedule with Algonquin Regional High School starting July 1, 2027.
key_details: Amends Article 29 (Retirement Incentive Program) of the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A contract.
Amends Article 22, Schedule A (Salary) to align Southborough teacher salary scales to the Algonquin Regional Teachers Association Unit A schedule.
The salary alignment takes effect on July 1, 2027.
topics.outcome: The committee voted 5-0 to approve the contract amendments to Articles 22 and 29.
topics.why_it_matters: Aligning teacher compensation with the regional high school impacts district operating costs, town tax requirements, and educator retention starting in FY28.

votes.motion: Accept the FY27 monthly general fund expenditure report through September 30, 2026, and approve the FY27 budget line-item transfers as presented
Approve the FY28 School Committee budget priorities as presented
Approve Policy J-220 on Medication Administration in Schools as presented

Amend the Southborough Teachers Association Unit A collective bargaining agreement Article 29 (Retirement Incentive Program) and Article 22 (Schedule A Salary) to align the salary schedule to the Algonquin Regional Teachers Association Unit A collective bargaining agreement beginning July 1, 2027

public_comment.summary: A resident of General Henry Knox Road commented on the Neary renovation options, urging officials to consider town-wide capital needs comprehensively and to compare Neary project costs with impending deferred maintenance needs at Finn School that are expected in 10 to 15 years.
